# Objects

An OBJECT is a canvas face the desk DRAWS. One WebGPU renderer draws every object
on the cutting mat straight from the document, and a KIND is the GPU program that
draws its own objects — its WGSL, its pass, its geometry, its pick. Whatever a
built-in kind can do, a plugin kind declares the same way (plugin parity): there
is no React component and no DOM under the camera.

The manifest owns the DURABLE half — the type name, prop names and group names
outlive any implementation — and names ONE export of the renderer module that
holds the kind. The host compiles the two halves into the object (`defineObject`);
plugin code never does.

## On the desk, today

Every door ACCEPTS the contract below: fieldd lists the plugin's kinds, `check`
activates it like any plugin, and the renderer compiles each kind through
`defineObject` before the desk's first frame. What no door does yet is LAY one: the
pegboard that hangs your `tray` entry is not wired into the desk's chrome, so nothing
a person can do puts your object on a board. `vibefield-plugin try <dir>` does it for
you — the app, on a fresh profile with your plugin staged alone, lays one object of
each of your kinds on a fresh board and says whether each is DRAWN (`cli.md`).

## Declaring

One entry per kind under `contributes.objects`:

| field | type | required | rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | string | yes | at most 128 characters |
| `title` | string | yes | at least 1 character; at most 80 characters |
| `description` | string | no | at most 500 characters |
| `schemaVersion` | number | yes | `integer; > 0` |
| `size` | { w: number, h: number } | yes | — |
| `minSize` | { w: number, h: number } | no | — |
| `interaction` | { selectable?: boolean, movable?: boolean, resizable?: boolean, snap?: `source` \| `target` \| `both` \| `none`, dragOn?: `press` \| `longPress`, solid?: boolean, sweepContained?: boolean } | no | — |
| `container` | `{ accepts: string[], provides?: string[], portal?: object }` | no | — |
| `provides` | `string[]` | no | at most 16 item(s) |
| `ports` | { id: string, side: `n` \| `e` \| `s` \| `w`, index?: number, accepts?: string[] }[] | no | at most 16 item(s) |
| `props` | object mapping name → one of `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `enum`, `json`, `entity-ref`, `session-ref`, `terminal-ref`, `artifact-ref`, `file-ref` | no | discriminated by `kind`; defaults to `{}` |
| `groups` | `object mapping name → string[]` | no | at least 1 item(s); defaults to `{}` |
| `behaviors` | `{ id: string, data?: object mapping name → recursive shape }[]` | no | at most 16 item(s) |
| `tray` | { category: string, label: string, order?: number, hang: object, props?: object mapping name → one of string, number, boolean, take?: one of `"face"`, object mapping name → one of string, number, boolean, local?: boolean } | no | — |
| `binding` | { kind: string } | yes | — |

- `type` is the durable name, `<pluginId>` or `<pluginId>.<name>`.
- `size` is what a new one spawns at, in world units; `minSize` bounds a resize
  (`interaction.resizable`). There is no size mode: an object is its size.
- `interaction`, `container`, `props`, `groups`, `behaviors` carry the canvas's
  durable vocabulary — Props and Conflict groups, below, say each in full.
- `provides` is what the DESK PLACES BY, never a type list: `desk.object` lies on
  the desk (declare it, or nothing places the kind), `desk.containable` goes into
  a mini mat (then declare `chip`, below), `desk.pinnable` pins to a calendar's
  day. A container's own `container.accepts`/`provides` use the same keys.
- `ports` are accepted and recorded; the desk draws no wire until the STRING
  program lands — a kind with ports hangs and places like any other meanwhile.
- `tray` hangs a specimen on the pegboard (next section); absent, the kind is
  placeable but hangs nowhere.
- `binding.kind` names the export (an identifier) that holds the kind — one name,
  read by the host, never registered from `activate`.
- `onObject:<type>` is an object's activation event — the plugin is activated no
  later than the type's first instance appearing in the document, independent of
  the kind's pass (the desk makes every registered kind's pass at its mount). The
  retired `onWidget:<type>` is refused by name (`onwidget-activation-retired`).

The old canvas face's view fields are RETIRED on an object and refused by name:

| field | where it went |
| --- | --- |
| `surface` | surface is retired on an object: its kind IS the face — the desk draws it, there is no dom or gl |
| `sizeMode` | sizeMode is retired on an object: an object is its size (declare size; resizable is interaction.resizable) |
| `preview` | preview is retired on an object: the tray draws the kind's own specimen (declare tray) |
| `category` | category is retired on an object: the tray's chip is tray.category |
| `defaultSize` | defaultSize is called size on an object |
| `maxSize` | maxSize never had engine support and is dropped on an object |


## Props

Props are the object's durable data. Each is one of these kinds:

| kind | fields | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `optional`, `mutable`, `default`, `maxLength` | — |
| `number` | `optional`, `mutable`, `default`, `min`, `max` | — |
| `boolean` | `optional`, `mutable`, `default` | — |
| `enum` | `optional`, `mutable`, `options`, `default` | — |
| `json` | `optional`, `mutable`, `inner`, `default`, `maxBytes` | `inner` describes the nested shape; the value rides one string cell |
| `entity-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |
| `session-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |
| `terminal-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |
| `artifact-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |
| `file-ref` | `optional`, `mutable` | an opaque host reference — the host resolves it, the plugin never parses it |

Every kind also accepts `optional` and `mutable` (default true). A default must
satisfy its own spec — an enum default outside `options`, a number outside
`min`/`max`, a string over `maxLength` are all refused at emit.

## Conflict groups

Props that change together belong in a named group. The name is durable: the
engine generates a component named `<object type>:<group name>` from it, and two
editors writing different groups of the same object never conflict.

- Omitting `groups` is the common case — ungrouped props join the engine's
  default `props` group.
- A group name matches `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, every member must be a declared prop,
  and a prop belongs to at most one group.
- An immutable prop (`mutable: false`) belongs to no group at all.

```ts
props: {
  title: { kind: "string", default: "" },
  body: { kind: "string", default: "" },
  color: { kind: "enum", options: ["amber", "slate"], default: "amber" },
},
groups: {
  text: ["title", "body"],   // one editor typing
  style: ["color"],          // another recolouring — no conflict
},
```

## The tray entry

The pegboard tray hangs what the entry says, drawn by the kind itself — a
specimen is the kind's stateless drawing of `tray.props` over the object's
defaults.

| field | type | required | rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | string | yes | at least 1 character; at most 64 characters |
| `label` | string | yes | at least 1 character; at most 80 characters |
| `order` | number | no | finite |
| `hang` | { w: number, h: number, accessory: `hook` \| `shelf` \| `clip` \| `rail`, pegs: [number, number][] } | yes | — |
| `props` | object mapping name → one of string, number, boolean | no | — |
| `take` | one of `"face"`, object mapping name → one of string, number, boolean | no | — |
| `local` | boolean | no | — |

- `category` is the chip on the tray's bar: a plugin's own string is its own chip,
  or name a built-in's (`paper`, `surfaces`, `things`) to join it.
- `hang` is how it hangs, and every entry says it: its size on the board in CSS px,
  the accessory (`hook`, `shelf`, `clip`, `rail`) and the pegs in pitches from the hang point
  (a pitch is the board's hole spacing; the hang point is the specimen's top edge's centre,
  its bottom edge's on a shelf — so a hook at `[0, -0.5]` sits half a pitch above it).
  Size it from the specimen: the board draws the object at its natural size scaled
  by the smaller of `hang.w / size.w` and `hang.h / size.h`, centred — so a hang of
  the object's own aspect fills it (ICE's note hangs 120 × 120, its whiteboard
  240 × 160).
- `take` is what one lifted off the board is made with: absent, the object's
  defaults; `"face"`, the specimen's props; a record, those props.
- `local: true` draws the specimen with the kind's desk state (a note's writing);
  absent, the specimen is the kind's stateless drawing.

## The binding — one export

The renderer module exports the kind under the name `binding.kind` names. The
export is the object's CODE half, `ObjectBinding`, from the SDK's object door
`@vibefield/plugin-sdk/desk` — the one door every name a kind is written against
arrives through (below, verbatim from the SDK's source):

```ts
/**
 * An OBJECT's code half (spec §12.8; DK-0f's contract): the value of the renderer module's NAMED
 * EXPORT that `contributes.objects[].binding.kind` names. Static, never registered from `activate` —
 * the desk creates every kind's pass together at its mount — so the HOST reads the export and
 * compiles the prefab from the manifest's DURABLE half through ICE's `defineObject` (§12.2: plugin
 * code never owns a durable schema). The host refuses a binding whose `kind` is not a desk kind
 * (`isObjectKind`) or whose registry `name` is not the row's type (one id, no second namespace).
 *
 * `defineObject` is re-exported by this door for a plugin's own TESTS (compile the object as the host will,
 * then read it back with `objectKindOf`) — never call it in the renderer module: the host defines
 * your type from the manifest, and a second definition of one type throws.
 */
export interface ObjectBinding<G = unknown, R = unknown, L = unknown> {
  /** The kind: its program (its WGSL, its pass) and its world half. Its `name` IS the row's type. */
  readonly kind: ObjectKind<G, R, L>;
  /** The props chain to the manifest's `schemaVersion`: version → (prev) => next. Renames of the TYPE are host history, never a plugin's (`TYPE_RENAMES`). */
  readonly migrate?: ObjectDef["migrate"];
  /** The hand onto the kind's state, made once per desk (a pen, a carry, a typing session). */
  readonly drivers?: DriverFactory;
  /** The kind's DOM half, declared: `lend` · `text` · `mount`. */
  readonly host?: ObjectHost;
  /** Selection-menu acts, one undo step each. */
  readonly menu?: readonly MenuActionDef[];
}
```

`activate(ctx)` stays the module's entry — commands, surfaces and behaviors bind
there as before — but a kind is NOT registered from it. The host reads the export,
compiles the prefab from the manifest's durable half, and registers the kind with
the desk's renderer before the first frame: every kind's pass is created together
at mount, which is why the binding is a static export and not a call.

The kind, whole (`ObjectKind`, from the door):

| member | required | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | the kind's registry name — it IS the object's type (the host refuses any other: `check` says `object-kind-misnamed`) |
| `stratum` | yes | `pads` \| `sheets` \| `things` — the desk's paint order: beneath everything (the calendar) · flat on the mat, holding a desk of its own (the mini mat) · every other thing (the note, the whiteboard, the notebook, the clock) — a card or a token is a `things` kind |
| `create(device, format, mat)` | yes | → `Promise<KindPass>`: the kind's PASS on the host's `GPUDevice` for the swap chain's `format`, on the root mat's pass (`MatPass` — the slot's view block, bound once, never written by a kind) |
| `reach` | yes | how far the drawing may reach PAST the rect, world units (shadow, lift, tilt): the desk culls the object only once its rect grown by `reach` leaves the view, and asks your `hit` anywhere within it — what `hit` answers is what is picked |
| `resolve(ctx)` | yes | the geometry `G` this frame, from the rect, the props and the flux |
| `record(G, ctx)` | yes | the record `R` the pass draws for that geometry |
| `hit(G, wx, wy)` | yes | the CPU mirror of the pass: `"content"` or `"frame"` is the object itself (a tap selects, a drag moves), any other string is a PART, `null` a miss |
| `chip(G, ctx)` | no | its far impostor inside a container's face — needed to go into a mini mat (`desk.containable`) |
| `frame(G)` | no | the silhouette the desk's marks go round; absent, the rect |
| `theme(palette, name)` | no | its look `L` from the host's palette, per theme — `ctx.look` |
| `local(host)` | no | its desk state (`KindLocal`: `tick` · `due` · `landed` · `forget`) — and the registered wake, below |
| `open` | no | what picking it up means (`OpenBinding`, quoted below): `extent` (the open rect), `pose` (`camera` \| `eye`), `tools` (the held bar's, each a `HeldToolDef` — `kind: "action"` with its op `run`, or `kind: "mode"`; with NO kind it is declared only, dim and never run), `readout` (its word in hand) |
| `rezoom` / `rung(ctx)` | no | the record reads the zoom continuously / only through a rung (a raster's band) |
| `face(G)` · `faceLaw` · `insideGrid` | no | a CONTAINER kind: the window its inside shows through, its chip law, its inside's grid |
| `reads` | no | components and tags beyond its props the builder journals for it |
| `composite` · `card` | no | a layered kind (its own target, laid once) · a CARD MATERIAL (quoted below): its objects drawn by the desk's one flat-card pipeline with its own WGSL — an option ON TOP of its own pass, never instead of one |

The pass (`KindPass`): `spawn(mat)` makes another slot's pass on the shared
pipelines; `prepare(encoder, slot, records, extra)` uploads this frame's records in
paint order and returns the count that will draw; `drawRange(pass, first, end)`
draws a run; `dispose()`. Optional: `records()`/`dropped()` (counters the host
reports), `idle(ms)`/`idleAt(ms)` (let device targets go when nothing drew),
`drawOver`, `endHold`, `tune`/`setLaw`, `cardResources`/`cardSlot`.

## The worked example — ICE's desk clock as a plugin

`examples/plugins/desk-clock` is ICE's worked third-party kind, ported to a VibeField plugin through
`@vibefield/plugin-sdk/desk` alone — the PARITY WITNESS: the product draws it beside the
desk's six built-ins, from a plugin. Its law, hands, zone and wakes are ICE's verbatim; the
code below is QUOTED from its source when these docs are generated, so it is the code that
ships.

The export that row's `binding.kind` names (`src/object.ts`) — the kind and its
selection-menu act:

```ts
/**
 * THE BINDING — the clock's kind and its selection-menu act (K8a — a plugin's act, declared as a
 * built-in's: the selected clocks' seconds hand flips, the first's deciding so a mixed selection ends
 * alike, each clock one undo step — with its own glyph, a stopwatch).
 */
export const clock: ObjectBinding<ClockGeometry, ClockInstance, ClockLook> = {
  kind: clockKind(),
  menu: [
    {
      id: CLOCK_SECONDS_ACT,
      label: "Seconds hand",
      keys: "S",
      glyph: { path: SECONDS_GLYPH },
      run: (api: MenuActionApi) => {
        const first = api.entities[0];
        if (first === undefined) return;
        const next = !flagProp(api.props(first), "seconds", true);
        for (const e of api.entities) api.setProps(e, { seconds: next });
      },
    },
  ],
};
```

The renderer module (`src/renderer.ts`), whole — the kind is an export, never a
registration:

```ts
import { defineRendererPlugin } from "@vibefield/plugin-sdk";

// The renderer MODULE (spec §10.1). The clock's code half is the NAMED export its manifest row's
// `binding.kind` names — `clock` — which the host reads off this module's namespace and compiles
// through `defineObject` before the desk's first frame; nothing about the kind is registered here.
// `activate` stays the module's entry, as for every plugin, and the clock needs nothing of it.

export { clock } from "./object";

export default defineRendererPlugin({
  activate() {
    // nothing to bind: the kind is a static export, and the clock asks for no command, surface or behavior
  },
});
```

The kind, whole (`src/kind.ts`): its program on the root's mat, the case resolved under
the desk's lamp, its hands recorded at the time it shows, its round pick, its chip inside a
container's face, the frame the desk's marks go round, its look, its desk state and its
opening — every name from the SDK's door:

```ts
/** The desk clock's kind, whole (`ObjectKind`): its program and its world half. */
export function clockKind(
  opts: ClockKindOptions = {},
): ObjectKind<ClockGeometry, ClockInstance, ClockLook> {
  const law = opts.law ?? CLOCK;
  const fallback = clockLook(CLOCK_PALETTE);
  const lookOf = (ctx: Pick<ObjectContext, "look">): ClockLook =>
    (ctx.look as ClockLook | undefined) ?? fallback;
  return {
    ...clockProgram(opts.text),
    reach: clockReach(law),
    local: (): ClockLocal => createClockLocal(opts.now),
    resolve: (ctx: ObjectContext): ClockGeometry => resolveClock(ctx.rect, ctx.flux, ctx.lamp, law),
    record(G: ClockGeometry, ctx: ObjectContext): ClockInstance {
      const style = styleOf(ctx.props);
      const seconds = flagProp(ctx.props, "seconds", true);
      const zone = stringProp(ctx.props, "zone", "local");
      const local = ctx.local as ClockLocal | undefined;
      const pin = asClockAsset(ctx.asset);
      let tod = SHOP_TIME;
      if (pin !== undefined) tod = timeOfDay(pin.at, zone);
      else if (local !== undefined) {
        // the desk's wall clock — and the clock says what it shows, so the desk wakes exactly when a hand must move (local.ts)
        const wall = local.now();
        const step = stepOf(seconds);
        tod = timeOfDay(wall + EARLY_MS, zone);
        local.saw(ctx.entity, step, keyAt(wall, step));
      }
      const hands = handAngles(tod, seconds);
      local?.show(ctx.entity, { tod, ...hands, seconds, pinned: pin !== undefined });
      return {
        geometry: G,
        hands,
        seconds,
        style: CLOCK_STYLES.indexOf(style),
        ring24: flagProp(ctx.props, "ring24", false),
        colours: lookOf(ctx).styles[style],
      };
    },
    hit: (G: ClockGeometry, wx: number, wy: number): ObjectHit | null =>
      onClock(G, wx, wy) ? "content" : null,
    // far inside a container's face (K8a's generic chips): a disc of its dial in the paper finish — a container that draws paper chips shows it
    chip: (G: ClockGeometry, ctx: ObjectContext): ChildShape => ({
      finish: PAPER_FINISH,
      cx: G.centre[0],
      cy: G.centre[1],
      hx: G.radius,
      hy: G.radius,
      angle: 0,
      radius: G.radius,
      colour: lookOf(ctx).styles[styleOf(ctx.props)].dial,
      height: G.heights.case * 0.5,
    }),
    // the desk's marks go round the round case as drawn (its corner its radius)
    frame: (G: ClockGeometry): MarkFrame => ({
      cx: G.centre[0],
      cy: G.centre[1],
      hx: G.radius,
      hy: G.radius,
      angle: 0,
      r: G.radius,
    }),
    theme: (palette: Palette, _name: ThemeName): ClockLook =>
      clockLook((palette as ClockPalette).clocks ?? CLOCK_PALETTE),
    // picked up, it is set: the held bar's tools are its own (a flat kind: the held slot's camera frames the case); its word in hand
    // is the time it shows (I22)
    open: {
      extent: (c) => c.rect,
      tools: CLOCK_TOOLS,
      readout: (c) =>
        clockWord(
          (c.local as ClockLocal | undefined)?.shown(c.entity),
          flagProp(c.props(), "ring24", false),
        ),
    },
  };
}
```

Its WGSL ships as `.wgsl` FILES (`src/clock.wgsl`, `src/clock-pass.wgsl`): plugin-build
inlines each into the renderer bundle as its text, and the program composes them after the
kit's pieces by name (`src/shaders.ts`):

```ts
/** The clock pass's program: the kit's view · portal · sdf · light by name, then the clock's record, module and entry. */
export function clockShaders(text?: ShaderText): ComposeOptions {
  return kitWgsl(
    ["view", "portal", "sdf", "light"],
    {
      structs: [Clock],
      modules: [{ label: "desk-clock/clock.wgsl", text: CLOCK_WGSL }],
      entry: { label: "desk-clock/clock-pass.wgsl", text: CLOCK_PASS_WGSL },
    },
    text,
  );
}
```

Its registered wake (`src/local.ts`): the desk asks `due` after every step and gets the
wall clock's next boundary a drawn clock needs — a frame a second with its seconds hand, a
minute without, none at all with no clock drawn:

```ts
due(now) {
  if (drawn.size === 0) return Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
  const wall = clock();
  let at = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
  for (const { step, key } of drawn.values()) at = Math.min(at, nextMoveAt(key, step));
  return now + Math.max(0, at - wall);
},
```

The rest is its own: `src/pass.ts` (instanced, a persistent record store, the slot's one
view block bound and never written), `src/layout.ts` (its GPU record, declared once),
`src/law.ts` (pure: the time it shows, the hands, the zone, the wake's arithmetic),
`src/theme.ts` (its look from the palette), `src/glyphs.ts` (its act's and tools' own
drawings) — and `test/imports.test.ts`, its wall: it names `@vibefield/plugin-sdk`, `/desk`,
its own modules and its `.wgsl`, never `@vibecook/ice` and never `/desk/objects`.

## What the kind receives

Everything a kind needs ARRIVES; a kind never reads the world or the DOM itself,
so the same kind draws for the app, a test's fake world and the Node oracle alike.

- **`create(device, format, mat)`** — the host's one `GPUDevice` (the renderer's
  realm, the host's device, at today's trust — see `context.md`), the swap chain's
  `GPUTextureFormat`, and the root mat's `MatPass`: the slot's view block (camera,
  light, frame — written once per frame per slot, bound once) and the mat's own
  silhouette. Kit WGSL pieces compose in by name (`kitWgsl(["view", "portal",
  "sdf", "light"])`): a kind multiplies by `portal_cover` and fades inside a
  container's face with no code of its own.
- **`resolve(ctx)` / `record(G, ctx)` / `chip(G, ctx)`** — one `ObjectContext` per
  entity per frame: `entity`; `rect` (centred `cx, cy, w, h`, world units — the
  builder converts from the document's top-left once); `props` (the group fields,
  cached from the change journal, never re-read per frame); `flux` (`lift` 0..1 in a
  hand, `hover`, `fade` 1 alive … 0 gone, `ring` always 0); `look` (your `theme()`
  result); `theme`; `lamp` (the desk's one light, world units); `view` (camera + box
  + dpr); `grid`; `dt` (seconds); `asset?` (a still the host pinned); `local?` (your
  desk state); `inside?` (a container's content bounds, view and chips); `held?`
  (the carry amount, whether to open, the eye kind's rise).
- **`local(host)`** — a `KindHost`: `pass()` your root pass; `use(key)` the SERVICES
  lent on this desk — the host's text raster (`TEXT_RASTER`), picture decoder
  (`PICTURE_DECODER`) and blob store (`BLOB_STORE`), and what any object's DOM half
  lends — always through this registry, never a host object directly; `children`
  (an object's data children, a board's strokes); `drawn`, `budget`, `rasters`,
  `remake`, `wake` (the desk's own doors — never lent, never replaced).
- **`drivers(host)`** — a `KindDriverHost`: the `world`, the document's doors
  (`docs` — facts are written ONLY through them, at a gesture's end), your `local`
  and `look`, `isKind`/`kind(name)`/`provides(key)` predicates (ask after a
  capability, never another kind's name), the builder's word (`geometryOf`,
  `heldToWorld`, `hand`), `refused`, `wake`. A driver is `follow(now)` once a frame
  before the kinds' clocks, `idle()` when it has nothing to follow, `dispose()`.
- **`host.lend` / `host.text` / `host.mount`** — the DOM half, in the layer's order:
  `lend` services only a browser makes (handed what is lent so far and a `wake`);
  `text` the object's TEXT PARTS that lease the desk's ONE editor (a part with `tap`
  is routed every tap; one without is leased by your own half at event time);
  `mount` a screen-space half handed an `ObjectDomHost` (`container`, `world`,
  `docs`, `use`, `editor`, `object`, `driver`, `look`, the builder's word, `wake`).
- **`menu[].run(api)`** — a `MenuActionApi`: `api.entities` (the selected objects of
  your type, in selection order), `api.props(e)`, `api.setProps(e, patch)`,
  `api.transact(fn)`. **A held tool's `run(api)`** — a `HeldToolApi`: the object in
  hand is `api.entity`, so `api.props()` and `api.setProps(patch)` take no entity;
  plus `api.transact(fn)`, `api.undo()`, `api.redo()`. Every write is ONE
  transaction, one undo step (`{ undoable: false }` opts out).

## Reading props

`ctx.props` is FLAT: every prop the row declares, by its name, whatever conflict group it
rides in, as the document holds it now (cached from the change journal — read it each
frame, never keep it). Read each with its type and a default, through the door:

```ts
/** A prop read with a type and a default — the kinds' one door to `ctx.props`. */
export declare const numberProp: (props: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, name: string, fallback: number) => number;
export declare const stringProp: (props: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, name: string, fallback: string) => string;
```

A colour prop reads through `rgb` (the CSS syntaxes `cssColor` parses, to sRGB 0..1). A
free-string colour prop can hold anything, and `rgb` never throws on what it cannot parse (a
named colour like `red` among them): it answers the desk's missing ink, `MISSING_INK`, and says
the string ONCE on the console — the object drawn and picked, plainly not the colour asked for,
and never a strike against the kind. `rgb(s, { strict: true })` throws, for a kind that would
rather fail on a typo of its own.

```ts
export type RGB = readonly [number, number, number];
/**
 * Parse the CSS colour syntaxes tokens.css uses — `#rrggbb`, `rgb(r g b / p%)`,
 * `rgba(r, g, b, a)` — into sRGB 0..1 + alpha. The swap chain is a plain
 * 8-bit format, so what CSS shows is what the shader writes.
 *
 * A string it cannot parse — another syntax (a name, `#rgb`, `hsl(…)`), a typo, or no string at all — answers `MISSING_INK` (the
 * desk's ink, opaque) and is SAID ONCE: a `console.warn` naming it, the first time a page meets that string — never a throw, so a
 * kind whose `record` or `resolve` feeds a user's colour through here draws in the missing ink instead of being struck for it
 * (petition I32; I24's ladder). `{ strict: true }` throws instead.
 */
export declare function cssColor(css: string, opts?: ColourParse): RGBA;
/** `cssColor` without its alpha: sRGB 0..1. An unparsed string answers `MISSING_INK`'s three channels, said once (`{ strict: true }` throws). */
export declare const rgb: (css: string, opts?: ColourParse) => RGB;
```

A boolean is `typeof v === "boolean" ? v : fallback` — the worked example's own `flagProp`
(its `src/kind.ts`) is exactly that. A menu act's `api.props(e)` and a held tool's
`api.props()` hand the same flat record; `setProps(patch)` writes the props you name.

## The kit's WGSL — what your shader is composed after

A kind's program is `kitWgsl(pieces, own)`: the kit's pieces you name, composed BEFORE
your own structs, modules and entry into ONE WGSL module (`object-kit-piece-unknown`
refuses a piece it does not carry). What each piece declares is in scope in your shader,
and YOUR module-scope names must not repeat its. Each piece's module-scope names, complete,
read from the kit's own text when these docs are generated:

- `view` — `struct MatUniforms`
- `portal` — `const PORTAL_CHAIN`, `fn portal_sd(p: vec2f, half: vec2f, r: f32) -> f32`, `fn portal_cover_one(p_css: vec2f, portal: vec4f, clip: vec4f, dpr: f32, grow: f32) -> f32`, `fn portal_cover_grown(p_css: vec2f, portals: array<vec4f, PORTAL_CHAIN>, clips: array<vec4f, PORTAL_CHAIN>, dpr: f32, grow: f32) -> f32`, `fn portal_cover(p_css: vec2f, portals: array<vec4f, PORTAL_CHAIN>, clips: array<vec4f, PORTAL_CHAIN>, dpr: f32) -> f32`
- `sdf` — `fn sdf_box(p: vec2f, b: vec2f) -> f32`, `fn sdf_round_box(p: vec2f, b: vec2f, r: f32) -> f32`, `fn sdf_circle(p: vec2f, r: f32) -> f32`, `fn sdf_segment(p: vec2f, a: vec2f, b: vec2f) -> f32`, `fn sdf_rounded_x(p: vec2f, w: f32, r: f32) -> f32`, `fn op_union_round(a: f32, b: f32, r: f32) -> f32`, `fn op_isect_round(a: f32, b: f32, r: f32) -> f32`
- `light` (also named `lamp`, `gobo`, `night`, `noise`) — `fn mat_zoom(u: MatUniforms) -> f32`, `fn mat_dpr(u: MatUniforms) -> f32`, `fn hash12(p: vec2f) -> f32`, `fn value_noise(p: vec2f) -> f32`, `fn srgb_to_linear(c: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `fn rgb2hsb(c: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `fn hsb2rgb(c: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `fn line_coverage(x: f32, spacing: f32, half_width: f32, px: f32) -> f32`, `fn grid2(p: vec2f, spacing: f32, half_width: f32, px: f32) -> f32`, `fn line_weight(u: MatUniforms, cell_px: f32) -> vec2f`, `fn mat_albedo(u: MatUniforms, world: vec2f, px: f32, frag: vec2f, bn: vec3f, ruler: f32) -> vec3f`, `fn linearstep(edge0: f32, edge1: f32, x: f32) -> f32`, `fn blur_ratio(ndc_z: f32, p: vec4f) -> f32`, `fn sample_blur(tex: texture_2d<f32>, samp: sampler, uv: vec2f, texel: vec2f, blur: f32, n: f32) -> f32`, `fn sample_gobo(u: MatUniforms, tex: texture_2d<f32>, samp: sampler, desk: vec3f, n: f32) -> f32`, `fn desk_of(u: MatUniforms, world: vec2f) -> vec3f`, `fn lit_desk(u: MatUniforms, L: vec4f, p: vec2f, h: f32) -> vec3f`, `fn lit_gobo(u: MatUniforms, tex: texture_2d<f32>, samp: sampler, p: vec2f, h: f32, own: vec3f, n: f32) -> f32`, `fn shade_mat(u: MatUniforms, albedo: vec3f, gobo: f32) -> vec3f`, `fn night_luminance(c: vec3f) -> f32`, `fn night_scotopic(c: vec3f) -> f32`, `fn night_mesopic(L: f32) -> f32`, `fn night_encode(c: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `fn night_mat(u: MatUniforms, albedo: vec3f, gobo: f32, noise: f32) -> vec3f`, `fn mat_colour(u: MatUniforms, albedo: vec3f, gobo: f32, noise: f32) -> vec3f`
- `ruler` — `struct RulerHit`, `const RULER_LEVELS`, `const GLYPH_PAD`, `fn ruler_line(d: f32, hw: f32) -> f32`, `fn ruler_in(x: f32, a: f32, b: f32) -> f32`, `fn ruler_digits(a: i32) -> i32`, `fn ruler_pow10(p: i32) -> i32`, `fn ruler_digit_at(a: i32, i: i32, nd: i32) -> i32`, `fn ruler_label(index: i32, mult: i32, exp: i32, k: i32) -> i32`, `fn ruler_label_len(index: i32, mult: i32, exp: i32) -> i32`, `fn ruler_band(u: MatUniforms, along: f32, across: f32, phase: f32, wraps: f32, lim: vec2f, turned: bool) -> RulerHit`, `fn ruler_ink(u: MatUniforms, screen: vec2f, frag: vec2f, glyph_tex: texture_2d<f32>, samp: sampler) -> f32`
- `book` — `struct NbUniforms`, `struct NbBook`, `struct NbCloth`, `struct NbPaperS`, `struct NbEnd`, `const NB_PI`, `const NB_GOLDEN`, `fn nb_sat(x: f32) -> f32`, `fn nb_clip(k: NbUniforms, P: vec3f) -> vec4f`, `fn nb_desk_at(u: MatUniforms, P: vec3f) -> vec3f`, `fn nb_hash(p: vec2i) -> f32`, `fn nb_vn(p: vec2f) -> vec3f`, `fn nb_fbm(p: vec2f) -> vec3f`, `fn nb_detail(period: f32, px: f32) -> f32`, `fn nb_cov(d: f32, px: f32) -> f32`, `fn nb_sd_box(p: vec2f, b: vec2f, r: f32) -> f32`, `fn nb_sd_fore(q: vec2f, w: f32, h: f32, r: f32) -> f32`, `fn nb_shadow(k: NbUniforms, B: NbBook, P: vec3f, n: vec3f, rot: f32, tex: texture_depth_2d_array, cmp: sampler_comparison) -> f32`, `fn nb_colour(u: MatUniforms, albedo: vec3f, light: f32, gobo: f32, noise: f32) -> vec3f`, `fn nb_cloth(q: vec2f, pitch: f32, px: f32) -> NbCloth`, `fn nb_ring(d: f32, r: f32, w: f32, px: f32) -> f32`, `fn nb_hash2(p: vec2f) -> f32`, `fn nb_design(B: NbBook, q: vec2f, w: f32, h: f32, px: f32, base: vec3f) -> vec4f`, `fn nb_paper_seed(seed: f32) -> vec2f`, `fn nb_paper(k: NbUniforms, base: vec3f, q: vec2f, dqdx: vec2f, dqdy: vec2f, seed: f32, tex: texture_2d<f32>, samp: sampler) -> NbPaperS`, `fn nb_ruling(k: NbUniforms, B: NbBook, q: vec2f, w: f32, h: f32, px: f32) -> f32`, `fn nb_cover_g(k: NbUniforms, B: NbBook, q: vec2f, px: f32) -> vec2f`, `fn nb_cover_albedo(k: NbUniforms, B: NbBook, q: vec2f, px: f32) -> vec3f`, `fn nb_endpaper(k: NbUniforms, B: NbBook, q: vec2f, px: f32, stacked: bool, dqdx: vec2f, dqdy: vec2f, tex: texture_2d<f32>, samp: sampler) -> NbEnd`, `fn nb_board(k: NbUniforms, B: NbBook, q: vec2f, px: f32) -> vec3f`, `fn nb_edge(k: NbUniforms, B: NbBook, q: vec2f, sheets: f32, side: f32, px: f32) -> vec3f`

The VIEW BLOCK every kind binds — `@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> u: MatUniforms;`,
written by the desk once a frame per slot, bound by a kind and never written. The fields
a kind reads (its others are the mat's own — reach them only through the `light` piece):

| field | holds |
| --- | --- |
| `u.cam` | the camera: `xy` the world point at the canvas's top-left (world units), `z` the zoom — CSS px per world unit, `mat_zoom(u)` — and `w` the device ratio, `mat_dpr(u)` |
| `u.view` | `xy` the canvas size, CSS px; `z` the grain's time, seconds; `w` the OBJECTS' presentation opacity — what every kind multiplies its alpha by |
| `u.box` | this slot's box on the attachment, CSS px (`x, y, w, h`) — what a kind culls against |
| `u.portals` | the portal chain `portal_cover` reads: each container face's centre and half extents, CSS px |
| `u.clips` | each face's corner radius and on (0/1 — a 0 ends the chain), beside `portals` |
| `u.night` | `x` the night's amount — 0 the day's light exactly, 1 full night — what a kind mixes its day and night colours by |

The conventions the scaffold's shader keeps: world units, y DOWN (the screen's own axes);
a kind's rect CENTRED (`cx, cy, w, h`); CSS px = (world − `u.cam.xy`) × `mat_zoom(u)`;
clip space = CSS px ÷ `u.view.xy` × 2 − 1, y flipped; in a fragment `in.clip.xy` is
DEVICE px, so world = `in.clip.xy` ÷ (`mat_zoom(u)` × `mat_dpr(u)`) + `u.cam.xy`. The colour
a fragment returns is PREMULTIPLIED, times `u.view.w` × `portal_cover(in.clip.xy / mat_dpr(u),
u.portals, u.clips, mat_dpr(u))` — so inside a mini mat's face it fades with no code of yours.

A record's GPU struct is `defineStruct(name, fields)` — its WGSL generated from the one
declaration, so the CPU and the GPU cannot drift; `kitWgsl(…, { structs: [It] })` puts it in
scope. Its field types, laid out by WGSL's own alignment rules (`defineStruct` pads as WGSL
does) — a `vec2f` first, scalars filling to 16 bytes, then each `vec4f`, as the scaffold's
record does, wastes nothing:

```ts
/**
 * A field's WGSL type — the scalars, the float vectors and the matrix, and a fixed array of vec4f (the portal chain's) — and how
 * it PACKS, by the WGSL host-shareable layout rules (`typeInfo` answers them; petition I31):
 *
 * - `f32` · `i32` · `u32` — align 4, size 4: one number (`i32` written `| 0`, `u32` `>>> 0`, a boolean as 1 or 0);
 * - `vec2f` — align 8, size 8: two numbers;
 * - `vec3f` — align 16, size 12: three numbers — a scalar declared after it rides in its tail (bytes 12–15);
 * - `vec4f` — align 16, size 16: four numbers;
 * - `mat4x4f` — align 16, size 64: sixteen numbers, column-major (four vec4f columns — what a projector matrix is uploaded as);
 * - `array<vec4f, N>` — align 16, size 16·N, N ≥ 1: 4·N numbers as one flat list (stride 16 — legal in a uniform block).
 *
 * The vectors and the matrix are f32 alone (no `vec4i`, no `vec4u`).
 */
export type FieldType = "f32" | "i32" | "u32" | "vec2f" | "vec3f" | "vec4f" | "mat4x4f" | `array<vec4f, ${number}>`;
```

BY NIGHT: a kind that writes its colours straight out draws at daytime brightness on the
night desk (the scaffold's disc does). Two ways to follow the night: pick your colours per
theme in `theme(palette, name)` — the `look` your record reads, `name` one of

```ts
export type ThemeName = "light" | "dark";
```

— or LIGHT your albedo as the mat lights itself, as the worked example does: the `light`
piece's `shade_mat` by day, `night_mat` by night, mixed by `u.night.x` (the gobo and noise
it passes are the mat's own plates, which its pass binds beside the view block):

```wgsl
// The colour on screen of a lit albedo: the mat's day chain, the night's, or between (a clock is lit as the mat is).
fn clock_colour(u: MatUniforms, albedo: vec3f, gobo: f32, noise: f32) -> vec3f {
  let day = shade_mat(u, albedo, gobo);
  if (u.night.x <= 0.0) { return day; }
  let night = night_mat(u, srgb_to_linear(albedo), gobo, noise);
  if (u.night.x >= 1.0) { return night; }
  return mix(day, night, u.night.x);
}
```

## Shapes the desk takes — ICE's own declarations

These types are ICE's, re-exported by `@vibefield/plugin-sdk/desk`, quoted from the
installed ICE's own declarations — doc comments and all — when these docs are generated.

**`open` — what picking it up means, and its held bar's tools.** A tool with no `kind` is
DECLARED ONLY — the bar shows it dim and never runs it: `check` refuses an op without one
(`object-tool-inert`), and a tool ICE would refuse at definition (`object-tool-invalid`).

```ts
/**
 * The kind's OPENING (design-015 §8; D4b) — what "pick it up" means for this kind. `extent`: the OPEN rect in the object's
 * own desk units, centred as its rect is and UNTURNED (the builder turns it with the object): a notebook's spread (twice the
 * case's width, left of the spine), a board's face, a calendar's month — what the reading size fits into the view. `pose`: how
 * the reading size is reached — `camera` (a flat kind, the default: the held slot's camera maps the extent to the held rect
 * and the kind draws at rest) or `eye` (a thing with height: the camera keeps the desk's zoom and the kind RISES toward the
 * desk eye by `ctx.held.grow`). `openness`: how far the kind's own open motion has come (0 shut … 1 open) — the put-down
 * flies home once it is under 0.35 and lands once under 0.02 (absent: 0, a kind with no motion of its own). `spread`: a
 * two-page extent that opens one page at a time on a portrait phone (Q-p); `page`: which of its two is in view there — 0 the
 * right (the default) … 1 the left, flux the view glides by (D3t-b: the notebook reads page by page). `tools`: the held bar's
 * slots (D3t-a: live — a mode or an action each); `tool`: the mode in hand when it is picked up, from its props (default: the first mode);
 * `swatches`: the colour a slot shows instead of its glyph (the board's four inks — the product's palette, through the look), read
 * with the anchor as `readout` is — a throw leaves the slots their glyphs, said once, never a strike (petition I24).
 */
export interface OpenBinding {
    extent(ctx: Pick<ObjectContext, "rect" | "props">): ObjectRect;
    readonly pose?: "camera" | "eye";
    openness?(ctx: Pick<ObjectContext, "entity" | "local">): number;
    readonly spread?: boolean;
    page?(ctx: Pick<ObjectContext, "entity" | "local">): number;
    readonly tools?: readonly HeldToolDef[];
    tool?(props: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>): string;
    swatches?(look: unknown): Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
    /**
     * The kind's WORD IN HAND (petition I22 — MC-D9's readouts): where the hand is, said beside its tools — the notebook's "Page 2",
     * the calendar's "September", a clock's time. A string, or read each time the selection's anchor is recomposed (the pickup, a
     * mode taken up, a held tool's act run — every frame drawn while it is held) and surfaced as `HeldAnchor.readout`; `undefined`
     * or "" — no word. A readout that throws is caught at the kind's boundary: the anchor keeps the tools and carries no word, and the
     * desk says so once — never a strike against the kind (petition I24: the anchor is read at the host's rate and only in hand, and a
     * word draws nothing of the desk).
     */
    readonly readout?: string | ((ctx: HeldReadoutContext) => string | undefined);
    /**
     * The WHEEL in hand (design-019 §5, M24 LT2): `"hand"` (the default — a plain wheel moves the object once brought close) or `"kind"`
     * — a plain wheel while it is held is the kind's, told as a `HeldEvent` "wheel" with its point (a page scrolls); the hand never pans
     * for it. ⌘-wheel and the pinch still zoom the hand, and past 0.72× still put it down. Carried onto the widget type (`heldWheel`) by
     * `defineObject`, where core's held input reads it.
     */
    readonly wheel?: "hand" | "kind";
    /**
     * The CURSOR in hand (design-019 §5, M24 LT2): asked while the object is held and the mouse is over one of the kind's NAMED parts
     * (any but `content` and `frame`) — a link's `pointer`, a text field's `text`, from what its source says (`LiveInfo.cursor`); the
     * desk shows it above its own (core's L4), written to the container only when it changes. `undefined` or "": the desk's own. One
     * that throws is a strike against the kind (petition I24) and the desk's own is shown.
     */
    cursor?(ctx: HeldCursorContext): string | undefined;
    /**
     * ESCAPE in hand (design-019 §5, M24 LT2): `"desk"` (the default — Esc puts the object down, in one press even while its kind leases
     * the editor) or `"kind"` — Esc is the kind's (a source that owns it: a terminal; its lease takes the key): the keymap never puts the
     * object down for it nor blurs the editor, and the hand is put down by Done, a click off it, or the pinch. Carried onto the widget
     * type (`heldEscape`) by `defineObject`, where the keymap reads it.
     */
    readonly escape?: "desk" | "kind";
}
/** One tool of the held bar, as a kind declares it (its `open.tools`). */
export interface HeldToolDef {
    /** Unique within the type: what `HeldTool.id` holds for a mode, what `ops.useHeldTool` names. */
    readonly id: string;
    /** Its name — the slot's accessible label and its tip. */
    readonly label: string;
    /** `mode` (the active tool) or `action` (an op, run once); absent = declared only (dim, inert). */
    readonly kind?: "mode" | "action";
    /** The keys that choose it while held: `KeyboardEvent.key` with `mod+` (⌘ or ctrl), `shift+`, `alt+` — "1", "e", "mod+z", "mod+Backspace". */
    readonly keys?: readonly string[];
    /** The key as the tip shows it ("1", "E", "⌘Z"). */
    readonly hint?: string;
    /** Its glyph (`HeldGlyph`, K8a): a name of the bar's set, or its own drawing (`{ path }`). */
    readonly glyph?: HeldGlyph;
    /** A mode chosen again while active hands the hand back the mode before it. */
    readonly toggle?: boolean;
    /** The cursor over the object's drawing surface (its `content` part) while this mode is active — "none" where the tool draws itself. */
    readonly cursor?: string;
    /** false: keys only — no slot in the bar (the board's tip, its wipe). */
    readonly bar?: boolean;
    /** An action's op. */
    run?(api: HeldToolApi): void;
    /**
     * Its STATE NOW (petition I49 — `HeldToolState`): asked with the anchor, as the kind's `open.readout` is, and when the tool is used.
     * Undefined — or absent — the tool as declared. One that THROWS is caught where it is asked (the desk says so once, never a strike):
     * the tool stands as declared.
     */
    state?(ctx: HeldToolStateContext): HeldToolState | undefined;
}
/**
 * A held tool's GLYPH (design-016 §5 · K-L2, K8a): a NAME the bar draws (its set — `SELECTION_GLYPHS` in `@ice/react`, which an
 * app may extend), or the tool's OWN drawing — SVG path data in the bar's 24-unit box, stroked 2 units in the bar's ink as the
 * bar's own are, or filled (`fill`). A plugin kind in its own package, which draws no React, declares its drawing; a name the bar
 * does not know is never drawn as another glyph (the bar marks it missing and says so).
 */
export type HeldGlyph = string | {
    readonly path: string;
    readonly fill?: boolean;
};
```

**`chip` — its far impostor inside a container's face** (with `desk.containable`):

```ts
/** One child as the face's far LOD draws it, in the CHILD's frame (the inside's world). */
export interface ChildShape {
    /** Its finish (`ChipFinish`) — or finishes, in preference order; the builder hands the container the one it draws. */
    readonly finish: ChipFinish | readonly ChipFinish[];
    readonly cx: number;
    readonly cy: number;
    /** Half extents, the tilt (radians), the corner radius — the child's own. */
    readonly hx: number;
    readonly hy: number;
    readonly angle: number;
    readonly radius: number;
    /** Its colour: the paper's, or the vinyl's. */
    readonly colour: RGB;
    /** How far it stands off the face, child units — what its contact shadow is cast from. */
    readonly height: number;
    /** A note's writing, GREEKED: the pen's colour, the text's left edge and em (note units from the sheet's top-left), and each line's baseline and width. */
    readonly writing?: {
        readonly ink: RGB;
        readonly x0: number;
        readonly em: number;
        readonly lines: readonly {
            readonly y: number;
            readonly width: number;
        }[];
    } | undefined;
    /** A mini mat's printed border, child units. */
    readonly margin?: number | undefined;
}
/** The two finishes the kit names — a chip's shared vocabulary (a note's `paper`, a mini mat's `vinyl`); a container may draw more. */
export declare const PAPER_FINISH: ChipFinish;
export declare const VINYL_FINISH: ChipFinish;
```

**`frame` — the silhouette the desk's marks go round** (absent: the rect):

```ts
/** An object's silhouette as the marks go around it: its centre, half extents, turn and corner — world units from a kind (`frame`), CSS px on screen. */
export interface MarkFrame {
    readonly cx: number;
    readonly cy: number;
    readonly hx: number;
    readonly hy: number;
    readonly angle: number;
    readonly r: number;
}
```

**`ctx.flux` — how it is held, hovered and present this frame:**

```ts
/**
 * What moves, per entity — the builder's springs, each 0..1 and SNAPPED to its target when settled
 * (the B7 trap: a spring that never quite lands keeps the desk awake forever). `lift` follows the
 * `Grab` fact (held), `hover` the local mouse pointer's exact hit (the B9 pairing — never the
 * dead-band `Targets`), `fade` the delete ghost (1 alive … 0 gone). `ring` is ALWAYS 0 from the
 * builder: the kinds' own selection ring retired at D4a (the marks draw the selection) and its
 * spring went at D6; the Node oracle alone hands a ring, for the baseline against the prototype.
 */
export interface ObjectFlux {
    readonly lift: number;
    readonly hover: number;
    readonly ring: number;
    readonly fade: number;
}
```

**`create(device, format, mat)` — the mat a pass is made on** (its view block, and the plates a
kind lit as the mat is samples: the gobo `silhouette` and the blue `noiseTexture`), **and the
record store a pass keeps** (`createRecordStore`: a record is packed into its slot only when it
changed — `pack` writes its fields and returns the block records it used, 0 without blocks):

```ts
/**
 * A SLOT'S MAT as a kind's pass reads it: what the slot lends every kind drawn in it — the mat's animated silhouette (the
 * lamp's gobo through the wind, this slot's own), the blue noise, the rulers' glyph atlas and its metrics, and the version
 * of those assets (a pass rebinds when it turns over). `KindProgram.create` makes a kind's root pass on the root's; every
 * other slot's pass is `spawn`ed onto that slot's. The ground's `CuttingMat` is the one there is; a kind never makes one.
 */
export interface MatPass {
    /**
     * The slot's ONE VIEW BLOCK (design-016 K-L3): a `MatUniforms` buffer the slot writes once a frame — the camera and box, the
     * clocks, the lamp's gobo, the night, the portal chain, the objects' presence (`view.w`; the mat's own is `presence.x`) — which every kind pass binds at
     * `@group(0) @binding(0)` as `u` (`kitWgsl`'s `view` piece). A kind never writes it and never keeps a copy.
     */
    readonly view: GPUBuffer;
    /** The slot's animated gobo silhouette (r8, PLATE_SIZE²) — what an object's shadow and dapple sample. */
    readonly silhouette: GPUTextureView;
    /** The blue-noise tile (NOISE_SIZE², shared by every slot). */
    readonly noiseTexture: GPUTexture;
    /** The rulers' glyph atlas (a 1×1 empty cell until a host uploads one) and its metrics. */
    readonly glyphTexture: GPUTexture;
    readonly glyphs: GlyphAtlasMeta;
    /** Turns over whenever a plate, the noise or the glyphs land: a pass holding a bind group over them rebinds. */
    readonly assetVersion: number;
    /**
     * The view block's bytes as the slot last uploaded them, and the key of what the silhouette holds (K7a): a layered kind whose
     * layer was drawn from the same bytes and key, with nothing of its own moved, lays it again without drawing it. Absent (a host's
     * own mat): the layer is always drawn.
     */
    readonly viewBytes?: Uint8Array;
    readonly silhouetteKey?: number;
}
/** How the pass packs one record into its slot; `blocks` (when the store has them) and `blockBase` name the slot's block. Returns the block records used (0 without blocks). */
export type RecordPacker<R, F extends string, B extends string> = (record: R, aux: number, into: StructBuffer<F>, slot: number, blocks: StructBuffer<B> | null, blockBase: number) => number;
export interface RecordStoreOptions<R, F extends string, B extends string = never> {
    readonly device: GPUDevice;
    readonly def: StructDef<F>;
    /** Slots at the start; grown by doubling up to `max` (65,536). */
    readonly capacity: number;
    readonly max?: number;
    /** The records buffer's label (`paper/notes`); the draw list is `<label> order`, the blocks `blocks.label`. */
    readonly label: string;
    readonly pack: RecordPacker<R, F, B>;
    /** A fixed block of `per` sub-records of `def` a slot (the mini mat's chips). */
    readonly blocks?: {
        readonly def: StructDef<B>;
        readonly per: number;
        readonly label: string;
    };
}
```

**`ctx.lamp` — the desk's one light; and the palette `theme(palette, name)` is handed** (the
desk's own roles; a host may hand more — VibeField's adds its pens, papers and inks):

```ts
/** The lamp over the desk in WORLD units: where it stands on the plane, and how high above it. */
export interface Lamp {
    readonly x: number;
    readonly y: number;
    readonly h: number;
}
/** The roles the ground paints from a product's palette, one token each, per theme. */
export interface Palette {
    readonly canvasBg: TokenRef;
    readonly select: TokenRef;
}
```

**`tray.hang` — how its specimen hangs on the pegboard:**

```ts
/** How a kind hangs on the tray: its size (CSS px), its pegs (pitches from its hang point), its accessory. */
export interface TrayHang {
    readonly w: number;
    readonly h: number;
    /** The holes the accessory plugs into, `[dx, dy]` pitches from the hang point — the top edge's centre, or the bottom edge's on a shelf. */
    readonly pegs: readonly (readonly [number, number])[];
    readonly accessory: TrayAccessory;
}
```

**`card` — a card material: an option ON TOP of the kind's own pass, never instead of one.** A
kind that declares one has its objects drawn by the desk's ONE flat-card pipeline, with its own
WGSL functions over its own records, so objects of every card kind interleaved in paint order are
one draw (without one, a run of one kind ends at the next object of another). It is not a way to
draw a card without a pass: the kind still makes its pass — `prepare` uploads the records,
`cardResources()` hands the card its bindings (a material whose pass hands none throws), and
`cardSlot(i)` hands the card each record it may draw, by its slot in the kind's records (−1, or no
`cardSlot` at all: the pass draws that record itself — so without it the card draws nothing of
the kind). The kind draws every object itself whenever ICE leaves it out of the card: when it is
`composite`, when its material names no fragment (`frag` or `fragInline`), when its bindings
would pass the device's limits, when a binding or card-function name is already another kind's
or a struct or module names like another's with different text (the kind registered first keeps
it, and a plugin registers after the built-ins — prefix every name with your own; the card's own
`u`, `gobo_tex`, `noise_tex` and `cards` are never a material's), or when its material does not
compile — that one alone said on the console. The door exports `KindProgram`, whose `card` is
typed by these two:

```ts
/**
 * A kind's CARD MATERIAL (K7b, design-016 §6 K7 — the run question). In mixed sibling order a run of one kind ends at the next
 * object of another (rig:scale: draws ≈ 0.3 × the objects drawn, at every zoom); the kinds that declare a material are composed
 * into ONE pipeline, so interleaved objects of every such kind are one run, one draw. Each object is drawn there by its OWN kind's
 * functions over its own kind's records, uniforms and textures — the pixels its own pipeline makes. The card's module is the
 * kit's pieces and every material's structs and modules (deduplicated by name and label), then its bindings, its `only`, its
 * card functions (`shaders.entry` — the same text its own pass composes) and a dispatch on the card's material.
 */
export interface CardMaterial {
    /**
     * The kind's program as its own pass composes it — the kit's pieces, its structs, its pure modules — its `entry` the CARD FUNCTIONS
     * over its bindings; asked when the card is composed (a host's text read then, as a pass reads it when it is made).
     */
    shaders(): ComposeOptions;
    /** WGSL the card composes that the kind's own entry defines otherwise (a texel read from its thumbnails alone — the card binds no pool). */
    readonly only?: string;
    /** Its bindings beyond the slot's view block and mat (`u`, `gobo_tex`, `noise_tex` — the card's), in its pass's `cardResources` order. */
    readonly bindings: readonly CardBinding[];
    /** `fn <quad>(slot: u32, vid: u32) -> vec4f`: corner `vid`'s clip position; (2, 2, 2, 1) — the degenerate — collapses a culled one. */
    readonly quad: string;
    /** `fn <frag>(slot: u32, clip: vec4f) -> vec4f`: the fragment's premultiplied colour through the slot's presentation; alpha < 0 = discard. */
    readonly frag?: string;
    /**
     * The fragment WRITTEN OUT instead of `frag`'s call: WGSL statements over `slot` and `in.clip` that set `c` (or discard) — the
     * kind's own entry's fragment, statement for statement. For a kind whose shade reached through one more function compiles to
     * other bits (the board's: one LSB on a pixel a scene — measured, K7b): the card then runs the very code its entry runs.
     */
    readonly fragInline?: string;
}
/** A binding of a CARD MATERIAL (K7b): the WGSL the card declares after `@group(0) @binding(n)`, and its layout (the stages, what it is). */
export interface CardBinding {
    /** Whole, after the attribute: `var<uniform> paper_k: PaperUniforms` — its name UNIQUE across every kind's material (a kind prefixes its own). */
    readonly wgsl: string;
    readonly entry: BindKind;
}
```

## Where logic goes

Three places, each for its own kind of state (the desk's law: facts in the world,
flux outside it):

1. **desk state** — `kind.local(host)` → `KindLocal` (`tick`, `due`, `landed`,
   `forget`): what you DRAW from flux and WHEN the desk must wake for it. Per desk,
   never in the document, never polled. A clock is this alone: its hands read the
   host's clock, `due` is the next second a drawn clock needs.
2. **drivers** — `binding.drivers` → a `KindDriver` per desk, ticked before the
   kinds' clocks: what FOLLOWS INPUT on one desk (a pen, a carry, a leaf, a typing
   session) — the hand onto your flux, writing facts only through `docs` at the
   gesture's end. Per view: two desks on one document have two pens.
3. **behaviors** — `contributes.behaviors` + `ctx.canvas.behaviors.bind`, attached
   through the object's `behaviors` riders (`contributions.md`): logic whose STATE
   IS A FACT the world must sync, undo or keep across views (`durable` data riding
   the object, `runtime` state every peer projects). Not for typing: a session's
   live text is flux committed whole at its end.

In short: drawn from time or a device → `local` with `due`; worked by hand →
`drivers`; durable or peer-shared logic → `behaviors`.

## Wakes — a desk at rest takes no step

The loop sleeps unless something is due, and a kind that does not say when it is
due pays the whole desk's idle. `KindLocal.due(now)` is asked after each tick:
answer `now` while a motion runs, a later time for a blink or a layer let go,
`Infinity` until a fact, an input or a wake moves it. **Absent while `tick` is
declared, the kind is due EVERY frame and the desk never sleeps** — the host says
so once on the console, naming the kind. Something that lands outside a frame (a
picture decoded, a tile printed, a detail fetched) calls `KindHost.wake()`; a kind
never polls for what an arrival can tell it.

## Checking it

One harness judges a kind everywhere: the SDK's kind-conformance harness
(`@vibefield/plugin-sdk/testing` — `runKindConformance`), with no device and no DOM.
`vibefield-plugin check` runs the manifest, wall, schema, artifact and activation rows
as for any plugin, and holds each object row to the BUILT module with the harness's
declaration and program checks: `binding.kind` names a real export
(`object-export-missing`) holding a desk kind (`object-kind-invalid`) whose registry name
is the row's type (`object-kind-misnamed`), hanging by a tray entry that says how
(`object-tray-hang-missing`, `object-tray-category-invalid`), providing `desk.object`
(`object-provides-no-desk-object`), its held tools ones ICE takes and runs
(`object-tool-invalid`, `object-tool-inert`); every name the built module imports from the
door one the door exports (`import-name-unknown`); its `create`, run on a RECORDING device that answers
every call as WebGPU does short of compiling, names only the kit's pieces
(`object-kit-piece-unknown`), asks for its shader as WGSL TEXT (`object-wgsl-not-text`)
that READS — entry points its pipelines name (`object-wgsl-unread`), bindings each stage
uses laid in its layout (`object-wgsl-binding-unlaid`), bind groups that fill their
layouts (`object-bind-group-mismatch`). NOTHING COMPILES IT: a shader naming what nothing
declares passes, and every kind with shaders carries the note `object-wgsl-not-compiled`
(`try`, below, is what compiles it). `plugin-playground <dir>` (`pnpm playground` in a checkout) runs the
same harness over every DECLARED STATE — each fixture in `playground/states.ts` (its props
validated first, `state-invalid`) × idle, selected, held, open (when the kind opens),
contained (when it provides `desk.containable`) × every zoom the desk's LOD names, and each
fixture once more at rest by night — through
resolve, record, hit (`state-hit-missed`: it must hit its own box), frame, chip, the
opening, prepare and drawRange (`state-spawn-failed`, `state-render-failed`,
`state-draw-ill-formed`), then dispose. A unit test calls it the same way. `inspect` lists
each kind with its tray chip, its hang, what it provides, its export, the states it is
driven through and, with `--json`, a `null` refusal.

SEEING IT DRAWN: neither compiles your WGSL. `vibefield-plugin try <dir>` does — the app
makes the kind on its own device and draws it on a fresh board: a WGSL error comes back as
the compiler's own line at YOUR file's line and column (`try-kind-refused`), a kind laid but
drawn nowhere as `try-not-picked`, and a kind drawn as `ok … DRAWN`, with stills (`cli.md`).

A STILL WITHOUT THE APP: `plugin-playground <dir> --still` draws each declared state on
DAWN — Node's WebGPU, the playground's own devDependency — through ICE's `createStill`:
one object of your kind on a bare mat, by day and by night, built as the host builds it,
its WGSL COMPILED (an error is the compiler's own line at your file's line and column,
`still-failed`), and judged: drawn (`still-blank` — it compiled and drew nothing), inside
its reach (`still-past-reach` — the desk culls and pads it by `reach`), steady
(`still-unsteady` — drawn twice, other bytes), and held to YOUR golden,
`test/still.golden.json`: each still's size and the sha-256 of its pixels, blessed ONCE
by the named flag, `--still --bless` (`still-unblessed` until then, `still-golden-mismatch`
after; `--bless --state <type>:<name>` mends one state). A GOLDEN IS HOST-SPECIFIC —
Dawn's bytes on the machine that blessed it (its GPU, driver and OS, and the playground's
Dawn), which the file records: another machine re-blesses locally and never commits over
it. A still lends your kind the desk's hand — the host's text raster (`TEXT_RASTER`: the
product's own faces, on a Node canvas) — and a kind that READS it is drawn with its
`local`, its writing as the product draws it (the row says `lent`; since ICE
`0.15.0-desk.6`, I35); a kind that reads no lent service is drawn without its `local`, so
a `local` that reads the wall clock never puts the hour into a golden (pin a time through
an asset). Whatever is said on the console while a still is drawn is
listed under its row, each line counted — under strata's DEV build (vitest, `node
--conditions=development`) too, where ICE says nothing of its own (since ICE
`0.15.0-desk.5`, I34, core's two `Tray` writers are ordered): a line there is your kind's.

WHERE IT RUNS: `check` runs the harness in plain Node — no `document`, no
`OffscreenCanvas`; the playground runs it in happy-dom — a `document`, still no
`OffscreenCanvas` or `createImageBitmap`; your own unit test runs in whatever
environment its vitest file declares. A `create` that reaches for a browser global its
environment lacks gets the note `object-create-not-run-here` (its states are still
driven, without its pass), so the two can say different notes for one kind — a kind
that needs a browser global says which in its README.

## At run time — enable, disable, update

A desk's kinds are the set it was MOUNTED with: nothing registers a kind on a live
desk, and nothing refuses an update. What the host does instead:

- **Enabled** — the desk REMOUNTS with your kind: on the same engine when this window
  had registered it before (you were turned off), on a new engine when it is new to
  the window — the same board reopens on it behind the veil, nothing lost.
- **Disabled, or removed** — the desk remounts WITHOUT it: your objects stay on the
  board, data and all, and wear the desk's MISSING face (a faint hatched card the size
  of the object, picked by its box); the selection bar names each one where its acts
  would stand — `Clock · plugin off` (disabled), `Clock · plugin gone` (removed) — and
  the status line says it once. Enabled again, they draw; until the desk has remounted
  with you, `remount to draw it`.
- **Updated** — your new artifact's kinds are compiled in a NEW renderer: the window
  saves its board, replaces its renderer and reopens the board with them. A
  `schemaVersion` bump runs your binding's `migrate` chain on the board's objects as
  it reopens; a `schemaVersion` that goes DOWN is refused by fieldd —
  `regresses schemaVersion` — and the live version stays. A type a board met before
  your plugin was here (a stub kept its data) is redefined the same way.
- **Its pack** — placing your kind needs its pack on the board, stamped when the board
  opens and when you are enabled. While ANOTHER desktop holds the board open the stamp
  waits — it would hold that desktop read-only — and lands at the board's next open;
  this desktop draws your objects meanwhile. A desktop handed a pack it lacks reopens
  on a stub for it and stays writable.
- **When it breaks** — a kind whose WGSL does not compile is refused at create; one
  whose world half throws is struck, and quarantined at the third strike. The rest of
  the desk draws on, your objects wear the missing face, `status().faults` names your
  kind once, and the bar and the status line say `can't draw`.
